morphology.shape: Oval budding yeast cells; forms pseudohyphae and true hyphae
morphology.arrangement: Budding yeast cells (blastoconidia), with pseudohyphae under certain conditions

habitat.naturalHabitat: Human gastrointestinal tract, oral cavity, vagina, and skin as commensal flora
habitat.hostAssociation: Normal commensal in most healthy individuals; opportunistic pathogen when host defenses are impaired
habitat.environmentalOccurrence: Primarily host-associated rather than free-living in the environment
habitat.reservoir: Human mucosal surfaces and the gastrointestinal tract

microscopy.stain: Gram stain or KOH wet mount
microscopy.appearance: Oval budding yeast cells with pseudohyphae
microscopy.arrangement: Budding cells, sometimes in chains of pseudohyphae

culture.media: Sabouraud dextrose agar (SDA), CHROMagar Candida, cornmeal agar for chlamydospore production
culture.colonyMorphology: Cream-colored, smooth, pasty colonies with a yeasty odor
culture.pigmentation: White to cream on SDA; green on CHROMagar Candida

identificationClues: Budding yeast cells on Gram stain or KOH wet mount
Germ tube positive within 2-3 hours in serum — the key distinguishing test

diseases: Invasive/systemic candidiasis and candidemia in immunocompromised or catheterized patients
virulenceFactors: Adhesins — surface proteins for mucosal attachment
Phenotypic switching between yeast and hyphal forms
Biofilm formation on catheters and other devices
clinicalImportance.transmission: Usually endogenous, arising from the patient's own flora; can also spread via contact or contaminated devices in healthcare settings
clinicalImportance.epidemiology: Most common cause of fungal infection in humans; a leading cause of healthcare-associated bloodstream fungal infections
clinicalImportance.labSignificance: The germ tube test is a fast, low-cost way to presumptively identify C. albicans among Candida species

examFacts.gramReaction: Not Gram-typed — a fungus, though it often stains Gram-positive-like
examFacts.importantDisease: Oral and vaginal thrush; invasive candidiasis in immunocompromised patients
examFacts.importantTest: Germ tube test; chlamydospore formation on cornmeal agar
examFacts.distinguishingFeature: The only common Candida species that is germ tube positive
